:JUDGMENT:
This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 07.06.2023 wherein the petitioners have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Sri Rajesh due to the impact of the accident.
2.

Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.4168/2023 It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the mother and petitioner No.2 is the sister of deceased Rajesh who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 07.06.2023 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the respondent's Tipper lorry.

It is submitted that on 07.06.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. said Rajesh proceeding as a pillion rider on Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LL- 4490 on the left side of the road near Ekhana hospital, Begur - Koppa road, near Prestige Apartments, Bengaluru, at that time, driver of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-3709 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle), came in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and dashed against the scooter of the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, Rajesh fell down and sustained severe injuries.

Immediately after the accident Rajesh was shifted to St.John's Medical College and Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein the duty doctor informed that Rajesh died due to the accidental injuries.

sentences.text: Consequently, on 07.06.2023 a FIR No.0099/2023 was registered with the Hulimavu Traffic Police station under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec. 134(a&b) and 187 of IMV Act SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4168/2023 and charge sheet was filed under Sec. 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec. 134(a&b) and 187, 66(1), 192(A) and 185 of IMV Act.
The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper lorry.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 33 Ningamma vs Muthu.S on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153803264/
2 years and was working as a computer operator and was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
3. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 denies that it has issued insurance SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4168/2023 policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.1 and denied liability to indemnify respondent No.1.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license.
The age, avocation of the deceased is denied.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. Vide order dated 09.02.2024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Rajesh R. S/o Rangaswamy was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred 07.06.2023 at about 5.30 p.m., near Ekhana hospital, Begur - Koppa road, near Prestige Apartments, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-3709?
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.4168/2023 2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Rajesh R.?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

4) What Order or Award ?
5.

In order to substantiate the claim petition, the claimants have examined petitioner No.1 as PW1 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 11 documents and the respondent No.2 got examined two witnesses as RW.1 and 2 and relied upon Ex.R1 to 4 documents.

Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 :

As per the Final Order for the following :
 SCCH 15 7 MVC No.4168/2023  REASONS 7.
Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the assertion of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-3709 /
offending vehicle.

8. In this regard the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and in her chief-examination she has deposed that on 07.06.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. while the deceased Rajesh who is her son was carefully travelling as pillion rider in Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LL-4490 on the left side of the road near Ekhana hospital, Begur - Koppa road, near Prestige Apartments, Bengaluru, at that time, offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner in high speed and dashed against the deceased

, as a result, her son as well as the rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries and her son succumbed to the injuries.
9.

The petitioners in support of their claim have in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts SCCH 15 8 MVC No.4168/2023 mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 8 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR which is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.134(a&b) and 187 of IMV Act on the basis of the complaint given by one Kirankumar on the same day of the accident, hence, there is no delay in lodging the complaint.

Further Ex.P3 spot mahazar and spot sketch discloses that the width of the road is about 40 feet and the accident has taken place on Begur - Koppa main road and towards the left side from north to south and the contents of the documents discloses that the driver of the offending vehicle turned his lorry to the right side and it came with the contact with the handle of the scooter and when the pillion rider fell down the right wheel of the lorry went over the pillion rider resulting in the accident and later the driver of the offending vehicle left the lorry and fled from the spot.
Ex.P4 IMV report shows the damages sustained to the offending vehicle as well as the motorcycle which shows the involvement of the vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P5 is the inquest report and Ex.P6 is the PM report which discloses that the deceased succumbed to the injuries due SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4168/2023 to the impact of the accident.

Ex.P7 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.134(a&b), 187, 66(1), 192(A) and 185 of IMV Act on the charges that the offending vehicle did Ningamma vs Muthu.S on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153803264/
4 not have valid permit
and charge sheet is also filed against the rider of the scooter for having consumed alcohol.
As far as the consumed alcohol is concerned the charge sheet is filed against the rider of the TVS scooter for having consumed alcohol.
However, deceased in this case is a pillion rider and hence the question of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased he being a pillion rider does not arise.
Hence, the charge sheet documents discloses that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Furthermore there is no clinching evidence to show that proportion of alcohol was to such an extent which was likely to impact his driving and the consumption of alcohol has contributed to the happening of the accident which otherwise would not have occurred.

However, the charge sheet document discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the rider of the TVS scooter only for SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4168/2023 consumption of alcohol on the charge of drunken driving and not for the offenses under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC which goes to show that there is no charge against the rider of the motorcycle for the offenses under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

Hence, in the absence of any contrary evidence on the basis of the documentary evidence it is elicited that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

10. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned, PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 and it is admitted in her cross-examination that she has not seen the accident and her son was the pillion rider and motorcycle was driven by son's employer by name Vinay.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the deceased,
nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.

The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for SCCH 15 11 MVC No.4168/2023 the offenses under Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC and Sec.134(a&b), 187, 66(1),
192(A), 185 of MV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the death occurred in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that death occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioners and in the 'Affirmative'.
11.
Issue No.2: It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother and petitioner No.2 is the sister of the deceased Rajesh.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P9 to 11 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the deceased and Petitioners.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
Hence, they have a right to apply for compensation due to death of Rajesh in road traffic accident.
The Petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the sister of the deceased, they being the legal representatives of the deceased Rajesh have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Rajesh and also they have proved that the death of the Rajesh has been caused by negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled to the Ningamma vs Muthu.S on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153803264/
5 compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.

13. Issue No.3: Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 33 years.
Ex.P-11 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 06.04.1990.
The alleged accident has taken place on 07.06.2023.
Hence, by considering Ex.P11, the age of the deceased is taken as 33 years.
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.4168/2023 14. Income and Avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working as Computer operator at BBMP office, HSR layout, Bengaluru and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
PW.1 has admitted that she has not produced any document to prove the avocation and income of the deceased.
In the absence of any evidence to prove income and avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as per the minimum wages Act.

Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation as per the minimum wages the wages are ranging between 14,000 to 16,000/- and as such Rs.16,000/- per month is taken as the income of the deceased for the purpose of assessing compensation.

Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 16,000X 12 =
1,92,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,92,000/-.
15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration SCCH 15 14 MVC No.4168/2023 for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
If these determinants are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in these decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4168/2023 Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward to the point of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self - employed and was below 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. The petition discloses that petitioner no 2 is the sister of the deceased and since she is major, she cannot be considered as dependent of the deceased.
There is no evidence adduced by the petitioner to show why she should be considered as dependent of deceased.
On the other hand PW1 has deposed that she has done her degree and is at home.

By virtue of the judgment in SLP (Civil) Nos 22265-22266 of 2018 between Deep Shikha & Anr Vs SCCH 15 16 MVC No.4168/2023 National Insurance company Ltd and Ors. Hence the petitioner No 1 alone is to be considered as dependent of the deceased and entitled for loss of dependency.

entities.text: Deep Shikha & Anr Vs SCCH 15 16 MVC No.4168/2023 National Insurance company Ltd and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner No 2 on the other hand is only entitled for compensation for loss of estate and consortium.
17. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his mother.

Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependent at the time of the death of Ningamma vs Muthu.S on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153803264/
7 the deceased is to be considered.
As per the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India where there is sole dependent in the family,  of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
18. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his mother.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (supra),
since the deceased was a bachelor, the deductions towards the personal expenses would be 1/2.
In this Petition, the deceased was aged 33 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.16,000/- comes to Rs.6,400/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/- + Rs.6,400/- =
Rs.22,400/-).
20.
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 16.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that, if the deceased was bachelor, half of his income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

21. After deducting  of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.22,400/- it comes to Rs.11,200/- (Rs.22,400/- - 11,200/-) and multiplier applied is 16, (Rs.11,200/- x 12 = 1,34,400/-,
Rs.1,34,400/- x 16 = 21,50,400/-).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,50,400/- towards loss of dependency.
Medical expenses:
The petitioners have not produced any medical bills to show any expenses incurred in the hospital.
Hence the actual medical expenses incurred for the treatment of the deceased or any hospital charges are taken an Nil.
23. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate',
Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-,
Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder SCCH 15 19 MVC No.4168/2023 Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love Ningamma vs Muthu.S on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153803264/
8 and Affection'.

24. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned

the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

25. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has occurred due to the negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-3709.
26.
There is no dispute as to the existence and validity of the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.4168/2023 insurance policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.

As far as the liability is concerned respondent No.2 got examined the investigation officer as RW.1 and he has deposed that the permit of the offending vehicle had lapsed and it was renewed on 09.06.2023 and valid till 08.06.2028.
Hence, it is renewed after the date of accident and hence it is submitted that as on the date of the accident there was no valid permit to the offending vehicle.
In addition it is also submitted that on examination it was found that the rider of the vehicle consumed alcohol it was found to be 150 mg per 100 ml.
On this point RW.1 is cross-
examined by the learned counsel for the petitioner and it is admitted that the pillion rider sustained injuries to his face and leg and not to head.
RW.1 has deposed in his cross-examination that since offending vehicle turned towards the right side the accident occurred and it was not due to the negligence of the motorist.

In addition as far as permit is concerned, FDA, Chandapura RTA is examined as RW.2, who has produced Ex.R3 and 4 which discloses that the permit was obtained through online and valid from 08.06.2023 to 08.06.2028.

On 07.06.2023 the offending vehicle documents have been SCCH 15 22 MVC No.4168/2023 transferred from Electronic city RTO to Chandapura RTO and as on the date of the accident there was no permit to the offending vehicle.
RW.2 has also deposed that since it is goods vehicle, the permit cannot be obtained in the main office.
Even though it is suggested by the petitioner that there is opportunity to obtain permit in main RTO, same is denied by RW.2.

Hence,
Ex.R3 and 4 clearly discloses that the offending vehicle did not have valid permit as on the date of the accident, hence, there is breach of policy conditions.

27. However at the same time the evidence discloses that it is not a case of non existence of permit but it is case of non renewal of permit and hence it is not a breach which has a fundamental impact on the occurrence of the accident or which would make the contract void.
Hence non possession of a valid and effective permit shall entitle the insurance company a right to seek recovery of the compensation paid to the claimants from the owner of the offending vehicle.

28. The learned counsel for the insurance company would contend that the accident having occurred after the amendment SCCH 15 23 MVC No.4168/2023 and hence the principle of pay and recovery is not applicable.

However there is no clear provision by way of amendment to indicate that the said Ningamma vs Muthu.S on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153803264/
10 principle is no longer in existence.
If the legislature intended to wipe out the said principle it would have made a clear provision to that effect.

Furthermore the contract of insurance is between the insurer and the insured and the intention of making statutory third party insurance is to compensate the road accident victims and their remedy cannot be abridged on the ground on of breach of policy conditions.
Hence they are entitled to obtain compensation from respondent no 2 who in turn will have to recover the same from the insured.
Hence the Respondent No.1 being owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
However Respondent No.2 will have to deposit the compensation amount and thereafter recover the same from Respondent No.1.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
29. Issue No.4:

From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation of Rs.22,83,500/- along with interest at the rate of SCCH 15 24 MVC No.4168/2023 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,83,500/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
 SCCH 15 25 MVC No.4168/2023  1) 95% to the Petitioner No.1

2 ) 5% to the Petitioner No.2  After deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of E-payment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 is meager, the entire amount awarded to Petitioner No.2 shall be released to her by way of E- payment and after her proper identification.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Immediately after the accident Rajesh was shifted to St.John's Medical College and Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein the duty doctor informed that Rajesh died due to the accidental injuries.
Consequently, on 07.06.2023 a FIR No.0099/2023 was registered with the Hulimavu Traffic Police station under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec. 134(a&b) and 187 of IMV Act SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4168/2023 and charge sheet was filed under Sec. 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec. 134(a&b) and 187, 66(1), 192(A) and 185 of IMV Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. Vide order dated 09.02.2024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Rajesh R. S/o Rangaswamy was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred 07.06.2023 at about 5.30 p.m., near Ekhana hospital, Begur - Koppa road, near Prestige Apartments, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-3709?
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.4168/2023 2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Rajesh R.?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
4) What Order or Award ?
5.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Ex.P1 is the FIR which is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.134(a&b) and 187 of IMV Act on the basis of the complaint given by one Kirankumar on the same day of the accident, hence, there is no delay in lodging the complaint.
However, deceased in this case is a pillion rider and hence the question of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased he being a pillion rider does not arise.
Hence, the charge sheet documents discloses that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Furthermore there is no clinching evidence to show that proportion of alcohol was to such an extent which was likely to impact his driving and the consumption of alcohol has contributed to the happening of the accident which otherwise would not have occurred.
However, the charge sheet document discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the rider of the TVS scooter only for SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4168/2023 consumption of alcohol on the charge of drunken driving and not for the offenses under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC which goes to show that there is no charge against the rider of the motorcycle for the offenses under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Hence, in the absence of any contrary evidence on the basis of the documentary evidence it is elicited that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for SCCH 15 11 MVC No.4168/2023 the offenses under Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC and Sec.134(a&b), 187, 66(1),
192(A), 185 of MV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
Hence, they have a right to apply for compensation due to death of Rajesh in road traffic accident.
Hence for the purpose of computation of claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,92,000/-.
16. The petition discloses that petitioner no 2 is the sister of the deceased and since she is major, she cannot be considered as dependent of the deceased.
There is no evidence adduced by the petitioner to show why she should be considered as dependent of deceased.
By virtue of the judgment in SLP (Civil) Nos 22265-22266 of 2018 between Deep Shikha & Anr Vs SCCH 15 16 MVC No.4168/2023 National Insurance company Ltd and Ors. Hence the petitioner No 1 alone is to be considered as dependent of the deceased and entitled for loss of dependency.
The petitioner No 2 on the other hand is only entitled for compensation for loss of estate and consortium.
17. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his mother.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependent at the time of the death of Ningamma vs Muthu.S on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153803264/
7 the deceased is to be considered.
As per the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India where there is sole dependent in the family,  of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder SCCH 15 19 MVC No.4168/2023 Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love Ningamma vs Muthu.S on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153803264/
8 and Affection'.
Hence,
Ex.R3 and 4 clearly discloses that the offending vehicle did not have valid permit as on the date of the accident, hence, there is breach of policy conditions.
27. However at the same time the evidence discloses that it is not a case of non existence of permit but it is case of non renewal of permit and hence it is not a breach which has a fundamental impact on the occurrence of the accident or which would make the contract void.
Hence non possession of a valid and effective permit shall entitle the insurance company a right to seek recovery of the compensation paid to the claimants from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Furthermore the contract of insurance is between the insurer and the insured and the intention of making statutory third party insurance is to compensate the road accident victims and their remedy cannot be abridged on the ground on of breach of policy conditions.
Hence they are entitled to obtain compensation from respondent no 2 who in turn will have to recover the same from the insured.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,50,400/- towards loss of dependency.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.
In light of the above discussion, the claimants are awarded compensation as follows:
Sl.No. Head Amount 1 Annual Income 16,000X 12 Rs.1,92,000/-
2 Future prospects 40% of Rs.16,000/- Rs. 22,400/-
 comes to Rs.6,400/-.
Hence the Respondent No.1 being owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
However Respondent No.2 will have to deposit the compensation amount and thereafter recover the same from Respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
29. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation of Rs.22,83,500/- along with interest at the rate of SCCH 15 24 MVC No.4168/2023 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,83,500/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
 SCCH 15 25 MVC No.4168/2023  1) 95% to the Petitioner No.1
2 ) 5% to the Petitioner No.2  After deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of E-payment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 is meager, the entire amount awarded to Petitioner No.2 shall be released to her by way of E- payment and after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
